**Solution 1** is incomplete and garbled. It ends with "Final answer: 79", which is not a probability. Its recurrence also treats the case where exactly one of Michael and James is selected as ending any chance of meeting. That is wrong: if the selected one wins, both remain in the game.

**Solution 2** sets up the right recurrence. Let P(n) be the probability they meet when n players remain, with both present. Then P(n) = 12/(n(n−1)) + [(n−4)(n−5)/((n−1)(n−2))]·P(n−3), with P(4)=1. I checked this and it gives P(7)=17/35. Substituting Q(n)=P(n)(n−1)(n−2) gives Q(n)=Q(n−3)+12(n−2)/n, so P(34) = (21 − 4S₁₀)/176, where S₁₀ = Σ_{i=1}^{10} 1/(3i+4) = 2476688353/4009205200. Carrying this through exactly gives 18571638947/176405028800 ≈ 0.105278. The solution's stated numerator, 18571639447, is off by 500, so its final fraction is incorrect even though its decimal size is roughly right.

**Solution 3** answers 1/2 by invoking an asymptotic "2/g" heuristic. It does not compute the exact value, and the true answer is about 0.105, not 0.5. Its own small-case checks (n=7 gave 4/7, n=10 gave 2/5) already contradicted the heuristic.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
